summary: Completed BREAK investigation and disproved both suspected causes with command evidence: current .dockerignore is effective and current Dockerfile layer ordering preserves dependency cache on source-only edits.
evidence: Hypothesis 1 (.dockerignore/context bloat) test: docker build --no-cache --progress=plain showed .dockerignore loaded (247B) and build context transfer only 1.46kB under current configuration.
Image content validation: container inspection showed ENV_ABSENT and GIT_ABSENT in /app, disproving current sensitive-file leakage via build context.
Hypothesis 2 (layer-order cache invalidation) test: Dockerfile order is COPY requirements.txt then RUN pip install, with source COPY occurring later in runtime stage.
Source-only edit verification: after a tiny change in app/main.py, rebuild output showed RUN pip install layer remained CACHED while only source-copy/runtime layers rebuilt.
Conclusion: both hypotheses are disproved for the current build configuration; prior slowdown and leakage symptoms likely came from an earlier Dockerfile/.dockerignore state.
